title: Bekhorot 59
description: Animal tithe by estimate and by thought, Rava’s hunt for a source that the tenth left in the pen is sacred of its own accord, the ninth mistakenly called “tenth”, and Rava’s rule that a tally fit to reach ten exempts, worked through fourteen lambs and a pen with two openings.
topics: 🌾 Teruma of the tithe, grain tithe and animal tithe: all by estimate and by thought
🐑 Rava: the tenth left in the pen is sacred of its own accord, and four baraitot tried as his source
🔟 The ninth called “tenth”: eaten only with a blemish, or non-sacred as Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says?
⚖️ The eleventh and the ninth: which needs the name “tenth” removed from the real tenth
📏 “Whatever passes”, not what already passed: a tally fit to reach ten exempts
🚪 Fourteen lambs, two openings: who is tithed, who is exempt, who waits for the next gathering
❓ Even a tally only possibly fit to reach ten exempts
🐏 Fifteen lambs: bring them all into the pen, do not pick out ten

a1.he: אַף תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר נִטֶּלֶת בְּאוֹמֶד וּבְמַחְשָׁבָה, וּמַעֲשֵׂר קַרְיֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא תְּרוּמָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי אֶת מַעְשַׂר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יָרִימוּ לַה׳ תְּרוּמָה נָתַתִּי לַלְוִיִּם לְנַחֲלָה״, וְאִיתַּקַּשׁ מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר דָּגָן, מָה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן נִיטָּל בְּאוֹמֶד וּבְמַחְשָׁבָה — אַף מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה נִיטָּל בְּאוֹמֶד וּבְמַחְשָׁבָה.

a2.he: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲשִׂירִי מֵאֵלָיו הוּא קָדוֹשׁ. מְנָא לֵיהּ לְרָבָא הָא? אִילֵּימָא מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁקָּרָא שְׁמוֹ ״עֲשִׂירִי״, לֹא קָרָא שְׁמוֹ ״עֲשִׂירִי״ מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה קֹדֶשׁ״ — מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

a3.he: וְדִלְמָא ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הוּא דְּלָא קַרְיֵיהּ, ״קֹדֶשׁ״ קַרְיֵיהּ! אֶלָּא מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא: קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְיָצָא הָעֲשִׂירִי וְלֹא דִּבֵּר — הַתְּשִׁיעִי נֶאֱכָל בְּמוּמוֹ, וְהָעֲשִׂירִי מַעֲשֵׂר.

a4.he: וְדִלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאִיבָּרַר לֵיהּ עֲשִׂירִי, אִי נָמֵי, דְּאַחְוִי עִילָּוֵיהּ!

a5.he: אֶלָּא מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא: קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וּמֵת עֲשִׂירִי בַּדִּיר — תְּשִׁיעִי נֶאֱכָל בְּמוּמוֹ, וְכוּלָּם פְּטוּרִין. מַאי טַעְמָא כּוּלָּם פְּטוּרִין, לָאו מִשּׁוּם דִּקְדַשׁ לֵיהּ עֲשִׂירִי?

a6.he: וְדִלְמָא דְּאִיפְּטַרוּ בְּמִנְיָן הָרָאוּי, דְּהָאָמַר רָבָא: מִנְיָן הָרָאוּי פּוֹטֵר!

a7.he: אֶלָּא מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא: קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּיר עֲשִׂירִי בַּדִּיר — הַתְּשִׁיעִי נֶאֱכָל בְּמוּמוֹ, וְהָעֲשִׂירִי מַעֲשֵׂר. וְהָתַנְיָא: תְּשִׁיעִי חוּלִּין!

a8.he: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:

b1.he: אַף הַתְּשִׁיעִי אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ, וְהַדִּין נוֹתֵן.

b2.he: וּמָה אַחַד עָשָׂר שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה קְדוּשָּׁה לִיקְרַב, אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הֵימֶנּוּ, תְּשִׁיעִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה קְדוּשָּׁה לִיקְרַב — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאִם נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הֵימֶנּוּ — אִין, אִי לָא — לָא?

b3.he: הִיא הַנּוֹתֶנֶת! אַחַד עָשָׂר שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה קְדוּשָּׁה לִיקְרַב, אִי נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ — אִין, אִי לָא — לָא; תְּשִׁיעִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה קְדוּשָּׁה לִיקְרַב, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ.

b4.he: אִי נָמֵי, אַחַד עָשָׂר, דְּאִיבָּרַר לֵיהּ עֲשִׂירִי — אִי נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ — אִין, אִי לָא — לָא.

b5.he: תְּשִׁיעִי, דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא אִיבָּרַר לֵיהּ עֲשִׂירִי, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הֵימֶנּוּ, תּוּ לָא מִידִּי.

b6.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מִנְיָן הָרָאוּי פּוֹטֵר. מְנָא לֵיהּ לְרָבָא הָא? אִילֵּימָא מֵהָא דִּתְנַן: קָפַץ אֶחָד מִן הַמְּנוּיִין לְתוֹכָן — כּוּלָּן פְּטוּרִין. מְנוּיִין גּוּפַיְיהוּ דְּאִיפְּטַרוּ — לָאו בְּמִנְיָן הָרָאוּי?

b8.he: הָהִיא לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ, הָא תָּנֵי: מִן הַמְעוּשָּׂרִין לְתוֹכָן!

b9.he: וְדִלְמָא מַאי ״מְעוּשָּׂרִין״? מַעֲשֵׂר דַּוְקָא, דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי ״יִרְעוּ״!

b10.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״יַעֲבוֹר״, וְלֹא שֶׁכְּבָר עָבַר. מַאי שֶׁכְּבָר עָבַר? אִי דְּעַשַּׂר עִילָּוַיְיהוּ — צְרִיכָא לְמֵימְרָא? אֶלָּא לָאו דְּאִיפְּטַרוּ לְהוּ בְּמִנְיָן הָרָאוּי? שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

b11.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הָיוּ לוֹ עֲשָׂרָה טְלָאִים וְהִכְנִיסָן לַדִּיר, וּמָנֶה חֲמִשָּׁה, וּמֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶם — אִם מִן הַמְּנוּיִים מֵת — מוֹנֶה וּמַשְׁלִים עֲלֵיהֶם, וְאִם מִשֶּׁאֵינָן מְנוּיִים מֵת — מְנוּיִים פְּטוּרִין, וְשֶׁאֵינָן מְנוּיִים מִצְטָרְפִין לַגּוֹרֶן אַחֵר.

b12.he: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָיוּ לוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר טְלָאִים וְהִכְנִיסָן לְדִיר, וְיָצְאוּ שִׁשָּׁה בְּפֶתַח זֶה, וְאַרְבָּעָה בְּפֶתַח זֶה, וְאַרְבָּעָה נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ שָׁם. אוֹתָם אַרְבָּעָה, אִם בְּפֶתַח הַשִּׁשָּׁה יָצְאוּ — נוֹטֵל אֶחָד מֵהֶם, וְהַשְּׁאָר מִצְטָרְפִין לְגוֹרֶן אַחֵר;

b13.he: וְאִם לָאו — שִׁשָּׁה פְּטוּרִין, וְאַרְבָּעָה אַרְבְּעָה מִצְטָרְפִין לְגוֹרֶן אַחֵר.

b14.he: יָצְאוּ אַרְבָּעָה בְּפֶתַח זֶה, וְשִׁשָּׁה בְּפֶתַח זֶה, וְנִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ שָׁם אַרְבָּעָה — אִם אוֹתָם אַרְבָּעָה בְּפֶתַח הַשִּׁשָּׁה יָצְאוּ — נוֹטֵל מֵהֶם אֶחָד, וְהַשְּׁאָר פְּטוּרִים; וְאִם לָאו — אַרְבָּעָה וְשִׁשָּׁה פְּטוּרִים, וְאַרְבָּעָה מִצְטָרְפִין לְגוֹרֶן אַחֵר.

b15.he: יָצְאוּ אַרְבָּעָה בְּפֶתַח זֶה, וְאַרְבָּעָה בְּפֶתַח זֶה, וְנִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ שָׁם שִׁשָּׁה — אִם אוֹתָן שִׁשָּׁה יָצְאוּ בְּפֶתַח אֶחָד — נוֹטֵל מֵהֶם אֶחָד וְהַשְּׁאָר פְּטוּרִים; וְאִם לָאו — אַרְבָּעָה פְּטוּרִים, וְשִׁשָּׁה מִצְטָרְפִין לְגוֹרֶן אַחֵר.

b16.he: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּמִנְיָן הָרָאוּי פּוֹטֵר? וְהָאַמְרַהּ רָבָא חֲדָא זִמְנָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: וַדַּאי מִנְיָן הָרָאוּי אָמְרִינַן, סְפֵק מִנְיָן הָרָאוּי, דַּחֲזֵי לְהָכָא וְדַחֲזֵי לְהָכָא — לָא אָמְרִינַן, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b17.he: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָיוּ לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר טְלָאִים, לֹא יֹאמַר: אֶבְרוֹר עֲשָׂרָה וְאַכְנִיסֵם לַדִּיר וְאֶטּוֹל מֵהֶם אֶחָד, וְהַשְּׁאָר פְּטוּרִים, אֶלָּא כּוֹנְסָן לַדִּיר, וּמוֹצִיא עֲשָׂרָה, וְנוֹטֵל מֵהֶם אֶחָד, וְהַשְּׁאָר מִצְטָרְפִין לְגוֹרֶן אַחֵר. תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: הָיוּ לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר טְלָאִים,

messages.text: Continued from 58b: to explain why Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, counts an animal taken from ten without counting as tithe, the Gemara cited Abba Elazar ben Gomel: “your teruma” speaks of two terumot, and just as standard teruma is taken by estimate and by thought,
Gemara
so too, teruma of the tithe may be taken by estimate and by thought.

notes.dh: אף תרומת מעשר נטלת באומד ובמחשבה
notes.he: וא"ת והא עיקר מחשבה בתרומת מעשר כתיב דכתיב ונחשב לכם תרומתכם והאי קרא בלוים כתיב י"ל כדכתיב כדגן מן הגורן דהיינו תרומה גדולה דמשמע דגן שישראל מפריש מגורנו משמע שפשוט לו יותר בתרומה גדולה ובגיטין (דף לא.) פ"ה הא דיליף תרומת מעשר מתרומה גדולה לענין אומד הוא דיליף אבל מחשבה ילפינן בתרוייהו מונחשב ונראה דרבנן לא פליגי אאבא אלעזר לענין מחשבה אלא לענין אומד ואת"ל דפליגי שמא יש בו שום טעם דלא מוקמי ממשנה בתרומת מעשר אע"ג דכתיב בגופיה כדאשכחן לענין מוקף כדאמר בירושלמי פרק שני (דקראוה כל התרומה כולה מלמדה ולימדה) חוץ מתרומת מעשר שמלמדת ואינה למידה דבתרומת מעשר כתיב ממנו לומר דבעינן מוקף ומוקמינן ליה בתרומה גדולה ולא בתרומת מעשר דבמס' בכורים (פ"ב מ"ה) תנן תרומת מעשר שוה לבכורים בשתי דרכים נטלת מן הטהור על הטמא ושלא מן המוקף כבכורים והא דפריך בפ' כל הגט (גיטין דף ל:) גבי תרומת מעשר וכי נחשדו חברים לתרום שלא מן המוקף מעמיד ר"ת מדבריהם דמדאורייתא לא בעי מוקף ומיהו נראה דלענין מחשבה לא פליגי מדפריך בריש האיש מקדש (קדושין דף מא:) גבי הא דיליף שליחות מתרומה מה לתרומה שכן נטלת במחשבה משמע דלכולי עלמא פריך והיינו תרומת מעשר דכתיב בה אתם גם אתם ומיהו לפי מה שפי' הקונטרס במחשבה פליגי דמשום מחשבה מוקי ר' יוסי בר' יהודה בשמעתין כאבא אלעזר בן גמלא ומתוך פירושו משתמע דאפילו בתרומה גדולה לית להו מחשבה דאי אית להו מחשבה לא הוה צריך למימר דסבר כאבא אלעזר בן גמלא דאפילו לרבנן נמי מצינו למילף מחשבה במעשר מדקרייה רחמנא תרומה ומיהו מצי למימר דמשום תרומת מעשר שבו קרייה רחמנא תרומה:
notes.en: In brief: Teruma of the tithe too is taken by estimate and by thought. Question: the main source for “thought” is written about teruma of the tithe itself (“And your teruma shall be reckoned to you”, a verse addressed to the Levites), so why learn it from standard teruma? Answer: the verse says “as the grain of the threshing floor”, which is standard teruma, grain an Israelite separates from his threshing floor, so the matter is plainer there. Rashi in Gittin (31a) explained that teruma of the tithe learns only estimate from standard teruma, while thought is learned for both from “shall be reckoned”. It seems the Rabbis do not dispute Abba Elazar about thought, only about estimate. And if they do dispute, perhaps there is a reason not to apply the verse to teruma of the tithe even though it is written about it, as with taking from adjacent produce: the Yerushalmi (Terumot ch. 2) says teruma of the tithe teaches but does not learn, since “from it” is written about it yet is applied to standard teruma, and the Mishna (Bikkurim 2:5) teaches that teruma of the tithe, like first fruits, may be taken from pure for impure and not from adjacent produce. Gittin 30b (“were the ḥaverim suspected of taking teruma not from adjacent produce?”) Rabbeinu Tam explains as rabbinic, since by Torah law adjacency is not required. Still, it seems no one disputes thought, since Kiddushin 41b challenges the derivation of agency from teruma with “teruma is different, as it is taken by thought”, evidently according to everyone, and that is teruma of the tithe, where “you also” is written. But according to Rashi they do dispute thought, since our sugya sets Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda like Abba Elazar ben Gomel because of thought; that implies the Rabbis do not accept thought even for standard teruma, for otherwise even they could learn thought for tithe from the Merciful One calling it teruma. One can answer that the Merciful One called it teruma because of the teruma of the tithe within it. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: פ"ה נותן עיניו בצד זה לשם תרומה ואוכל בצד זה ואע"פ שלא הפריש משמע שרוצה לומר משום דכתיב ונחשב שרי לאכול בלא הפרשה ושרינן נמי בשתיקה על ידי נותן עיניו בצד זה ואוכל בצד זה וכל זה דנפקא לו מונחשב עוד פירש לשון אחר במחשבה מחשב ואומר ב' לוגין שאני עתיד להפריש ואע"פ שעתה אינו מפריש כלום ורוצה לומר דדיבור צריך והא דשרי בלא הפרשה קרי מחשבה ואשכחן נמי דקרי למחשבה דיבור כמו (ב"מ דף מד.) על כל דבר פשע דאמר לחייב על המחשבה כמעשה ונראה דבלא דיבור נמי הוי תרומה מדתנן במס' תרומות (פ"א מ"ו) חמשה לא יתרומו ואם תרמו תרומתם תרומה וחשיב אלם ובירושלמי מפרש טעמא משום ברכה ובמס' שבועות פ"ג (דף כו:) משמע בהדיא דשרי כשגמר בלבו אע"ג שלא הוציא בשפתיו דכתיב כל נדיב לב וקאמר תרומה וקדשים הוו להו שני כתובים הבאים כאחד ולא ילפינן מינייהו שבועה ובמה שאוכל בלא הפרשה אין קפידא דלכולי עלמא שרי בכ"מ אע"פ שאין מפריש עתה כדמוכח ההוא דהלוקח יין מבין הכותים דשרי לכ"ע אי לאו משום ברירה אי משום דחיישינן לבקיעת הנוד ויש מקומות דשרינן מעשר שני לצפונו וא"ת כיון דשרינן תרומה על ידי נותן עיניו בצד זה ואוכל בצד אחר אמאי אין מגביהין תרומות ומעשרות בי"ט הא תנן פ' נוטל (שבת דף קמב.) מעלין המדומע באחד ומאה ופריך והא מתקן ושני ר' אלעזר בר"ש היא דאמר נותן עיניו בצד זה ואוכל בצד זה ולהכי לא חשיב מתקן כיון דאפשר במחשבה י"ל מדומע שאני שכבר נתקן אבל תחלת תיקון לא שרינן מטעם דאפשר במחשבה ואפילו דמאי אסור לתקן בשבת כדמוכח פ' במה מדליקין (שבת דף לד.) ואע"ג דשרי ליה בנותן עיניו בצד זה ואוכל בצד אחר כדמוכח פ"ק דחולין (דף ו:) גבי ר"מ שאכל עלה של ירק בבית שאן:
notes.en: In brief: By thought: Rashi explained that he sets his eyes on this side [of the pile] as teruma and eats from that side, even though he did not separate. He seems to mean that because “shall be reckoned” is written, one may eat without separating, and may do so even in silence, setting his eyes on one side and eating from the other. Rashi gave another explanation: he thinks and says, “the two log that I will separate in the future”, though he now separates nothing; that is, speech is required, and permitting [eating] without separating is what is called “thought”; and we find speech called thought, as in Bava Metzia 44a on “for every matter of trespass”. It seems, though, that without speech too it is teruma, since the Mishna (Terumot 1:6) counts a mute among the five whose teruma is valid after the fact, and the Yerushalmi explains [the exclusion] as due to the blessing; and Shevuot 26b clearly implies it is valid when he resolved it in his heart, from “every generous heart”, saying that teruma and consecrated items are two verses that come as one, so oaths are not learned from them. Eating without separating poses no problem: everyone permits it, as in the case of one who buys wine from the Samaritans, which all permit but for the issue of retroactive clarification or the fear that the flask might burst; and in some places we permit second tithe “to its north”. Question: if teruma may be taken by setting the eyes on one side, why may one not separate terumot and tithes on a Festival? Shabbat 142a teaches that one may lift out [teruma from] a mixture of one in a hundred, and when it asks “but he is fixing it!” answers that this is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, who says one sets his eyes on one side and eats from the other, so it does not count as fixing. Answer: a mixture is different, as it was already fixed; the first fixing is not permitted on the grounds that it could be done by thought. Even demai may not be fixed on Shabbat (Shabbat 34a), though setting one’s eyes on one side and eating from the other is permitted for it, as shown in Ḥullin 6b about Rabbi Meir, who ate a vegetable leaf in Beit She’an. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: And this ruling of Abba Elazar ben Gomel’s also applies to tithes of the grain, because the Merciful One calls tithe “teruma,” as it is written: “For the tithe of the children of Israel, which they set apart as teruma for the Lord, I have given to the Levites for an inheritance”.

verse.he: כִּי אֶת־מַעְשַׂר בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יָרִימוּ לַיהֹוָה תְּרוּמָה נָתַתִּי לַלְוִיִּם לְנַחֲלָה עַל־כֵּן אָמַרְתִּי לָהֶם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִנְחֲלוּ נַחֲלָה׃ {פ}
verse.en: for it is the tithes set aside by the Israelites as a gift to GOD that I give to the Levites as their share. Therefore I have said concerning them: They shall have no territorial share among the Israelites.

messages.text: And animal tithe is juxtaposed to grain tithe, as is derived from the verse: “You shall tithe a tithe” (Deuteronomy 14:22; see 53b). Just as grain tithe is separated by estimate and by thought, so too, animal tithe is separated by estimate and by thought. For this reason, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, maintains that even with regard to an animal that was not counted, if it was separated as tithe the separation is valid.

notes.he: בריש פירקין (לעיל בכורות נג.) ואת מעשרותיכם בשתי מעשרות הכתוב מדבר אחד מעשר בהמה וא' מעשר דגן:
notes.en: Is juxtaposed: at the beginning of our chapter (above, 53a): “And your tithes”: the verse speaks of two tithes, one animal tithe and one grain tithe.

notes.he: פ"ה מדכתיב עשר תעשר כדאמרינן בריש פירקין צ"ל דלית ליה הא דאמר [רבא] לשנה הקשתיו ולא לדבר אחר ועוד בריש פירקין דרשינן היקשא אחרת והבאתם שמה מעשרותיכם לר' עקיבא ושמא לא אתקש אלא לענין הבאה מיהו לרבא קשה היכי מפרש טעמא דרבי יוסי בר' יהודה וכן בזבחים פרק ב"ש (זבחים דף מה.) דרשינן קדשי עובדי כוכבים אין עושים תמורה מדאיתקש תמורה למעשר בהמה ומעשר בהמה למעשר דגן ובמעשר דגן כתיב בני ישראל ולא עובדי כוכבים וי"ל לענין לעשר מזה על זה כגון ממין על שאינו מינו דהוי כעין חדש על ישן לגבי הכי דוקא אומר לשנה הקשתיו ולא לדבר אחר:
notes.en: Animal tithe is juxtaposed to grain tithe: Rashi explained, from “You shall tithe a tithe”, as we say at the beginning of our chapter. One must say that [Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda] does not hold what [Rava] says: “I juxtaposed it for the year and not for anything else.” Further, at the beginning of our chapter we expound a different juxtaposition, “and there you shall bring … your tithes”, according to Rabbi Akiva, and perhaps it was juxtaposed only with regard to bringing. But according to Rava it is difficult: how does he explain the reason of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda? Likewise in Zevaḥim (45a) we expound that the consecrated animals of gentiles do not make a substitute, because substitution is juxtaposed to animal tithe and animal tithe to grain tithe, and with grain tithe “the children of Israel” is written, not gentiles. One can answer: [Rava] says “I juxtaposed it for the year and not for anything else” only with regard to tithing from one onto another, for example from one kind onto another that is not its kind, which is like new onto old.

notes.he: דכתיב עשר תעשר בשתי מעשרות הכתוב מדבר כו'. ובסיפרי כתוב ונחשב לכם תרומתכם ולא כתיב בב' תרומות הכתוב מדבר אלא כשם שתרומה גדולה ניטלת במדה ובמחשבה כך תרומת מעשר:
notes.en: And animal tithe is juxtaposed to grain tithe: as it is written, “You shall tithe a tithe”: the verse speaks of two tithes, and so on. And in the Sifrei it is written: “And your teruma shall be reckoned to you” [“your teruma”, and not “the teruma”]: the verse speaks of two terumot, and so on. Just as standard teruma is taken by measure [our daf: by estimate] and by thought, so too teruma of the tithe.

messages.text: If one counted nine animals and the tenth animal remains in the pen, it is sacred as the animal tithe of its own accord, even if it does not leave the pen and was not counted.

notes.he: שאם מנה עשר ונשתייר עשירי בדיר אע"פ שלא יצא ולא מנאו קדוש מאליו:
notes.en: Sacred of its own accord: if he counted the ten [that is, counted toward the tenth] and the tenth was left in the pen, even though it did not come out and he did not count it, it is sacred of its own accord.

notes.he: אפילו לא קראו עשירי ולא קדש:
notes.en: It is sacred of its own accord: even if he did not call it “tenth” and did not call it “sacred”.

messages.text: From where does Rava derive this halakha? If we say he derives it from that which is taught in the aforementioned baraita, this is problematic. The Gemara cites the baraita again:
messages.quote: the tenth animal remains in the pen, it is sacred

messages.text: And I have derived only that an animal that one explicitly called by the name of the tenth one is the animal tithe. From where do I derive that the tenth animal is sanctified even if one did not explicitly call it the tenth one? The verse states: “The tenth shall be sacred,” i.e., it shall be sacred in any case, even if it was not called the tenth.

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

messages.text: The suggestion is that Rava understands from here that the tenth is sacred even if it was not counted, provided there was a counting. Consequently, it makes no difference whether or not the owner called it the tenth or left it in the pen.
But perhaps this baraita is referring specifically to a case where he did not call that animal the tenth, but he did call it sanctified.
messages.quote: even if one did not explicitly call it the tenth one

notes.he: דליהוי ליה דין מעשר להעלותו לירושלים ולהקריבו אלא קדוש גרידא קרייה רחמנא דקדושה חלה עליו ואינו נאכל אלא במומו. ענין אחר ודילמא עשירי לא קרייה שלא קרא שמו עשירי אלא קדש קרא שמו ולהכי הוי מעשר אבל היכא דלא קראו כלל לא ליהוי קדוש כשאר מעשר. ולא מפי המורה:
notes.en: But perhaps it is “tenth” that he did not call it: [a first explanation:] the Merciful One did not call it “tenth”, so as to give it the law of tithe, to be taken up to Jerusalem and sacrificed; the Merciful One called it merely “sacred”, meaning that sanctity takes effect on it and it is eaten only with its blemish. Another explanation: “but perhaps he did not call it tenth”: he did not give it the name “tenth”, but did call it “sacred”, and that is why it is tithe; but where he did not name it at all, it would not be sacred like other tithe. This [second explanation] is not from the mouth of my teacher.

messages.text: Rather, the Gemara suggests that Rava derives it from that which is taught in a baraita:

If one erred and called the ninth animal the tenth, and the tenth animal emerged from the pen but the owner did not speak, the ninth animal is not sanctified and is not brought as an offering. But since it was called the tenth, it may be eaten only once it develops a blemish. And the tenth animal is the animal tithe.
It is possible that Rava maintains that just as the tenth is sacred in this case, when the owner remained silent, the same applies if he left it in the pen.

But perhaps it is different there, as the tenth animal was selected when it emerged from the pen, despite the fact that it was not counted verbally. Alternatively, the reason it is sanctified is that he pointed at it as it emerged, although he did not explicitly say that it was the tenth animal. Conversely, in a case where it remained in the pen perhaps it does not have any sanctity at all.
messages.quote: and the tenth animal emerged from the pen but the owner did not speak

notes.he: שלפי שיצא בסוף תשעה נברר מעצמו שהוא עשירי ולכך הוי כשאר מעשר אע"פ שלא קרא עליו שם. אי נמי ברייתא קמיירי כגון דאחוי עליה כשיצא הראה עליו באצבעו שיהא מעשר אלא שלא דבר בפיו. אבל היכא דנשתייר בדיר ולא קרא לו שם לא שמעינן אכתי דליהוי קדוש כשאר מעשר:
notes.en: That the tenth was selected for him: since it came out at the end of nine, it is selected of itself as the tenth, so it is like other tithe even though he did not name it. Alternatively, the baraita deals with a case where he pointed at it: when it came out he pointed at it with his finger to make it tithe, only he did not speak with his mouth. But where it was left in the pen and he did not name it, we have not yet heard that it is sacred like other tithe.

notes.he: שיצא חוץ ולא קראו אחד אלא שתק:
notes.en: That the tenth was selected for him: it went outside, and he did not call it anything but was silent.

notes.he: שרמז בידו [עליו] שהוא עשירי:
notes.en: Alternatively, that he pointed at it: he signaled with his hand [at it] that it is the tenth.

messages.text: Rather, the Gemara suggests that Rava derives his halakha from that which is taught in a baraita:

If one erred and called the ninth animal the tenth, and the tenth animal died in the pen, the ninth animal may be eaten only once it develops a blemish, and all the other animals are exempt from having to be tithed again.

notes.he: הואיל וקראו עשירי דתמורת שם מעשר מקדש לפניו ולאחריו כדלקמן אבל האחרים מיהא לא נפטרו אז הואיל והוא תשיעי למנין הבהמות:
notes.en: The ninth is eaten with its blemish: since he called it “tenth”, for exchanging the name of tithe sanctifies [the animals] before it and after it, as below [60a]. But the others, at any rate, were not exempted then, since it is the ninth in the count of the animals.

notes.he: השמונה שיצאו כבר:
notes.en: And all are exempt: the eight that had already come out.

messages.text: What is the reason that all the other animals are exempt? Is it not because the tenth animal is sanctified of its own accord, even without emerging from the pen?
messages.quote: and all the other animals are exempt

notes.he: מאליו בדיר אע"פ שלא יצא:
notes.en: That the tenth became sacred: of its own accord, in the pen, even though it did not come out.

messages.text: But perhaps the other animals are exempt because they were counted in a tally that is fit to reach ten. As doesn’t Rava say: A tally fit to reach ten exempts from the obligation of tithe?
messages.quote: the tenth animal is sanctified of its own accord

notes.he: כשיצאו תשעה בפתח היה שם מנין הראוי לעשר שעדיין היה עשירי קיים שהיה ראוי לצאת אחריהם ולפוטרן וכיון דראוי לצאת דמי כמאן דיצא כבר ופטר את המנין ולקמן מפרש טעמא אבל איהו גופיה מיהא לא הוה קדוש עד שיצא:
notes.en: Through a fit tally: when nine came out through the opening there was a count there fit to be tithed, for the tenth still existed and was fit to come out after them and exempt them; and since it was fit to come out, it is as though it had already come out and exempted the count. The reason is explained below [59b]. But the tenth itself, at any rate, was not sacred until it came out.

notes.he: שכשיצאו אלו עדיין היה העשירי שבדיר חי והיה ראוי להשלים מנינו ומשום הכי פטירי ולא משום שיהו מעושרין ודאי:
notes.en: But perhaps they were exempted through a fit tally: when these came out, the tenth in the pen was still alive and fit to complete their count. That is why they are exempt, and not because they are definitely tithed.

messages.text: If one began counting lambs for the purpose of tithing and at that stage the group was fit to be tithed, but ultimately he was unable to separate the tithe, e.g., if one of the animals died and there were only nine left, those that were counted while the tally was fit to reach ten are exempt from being tithed. Moreover, the owner is not required to include them in the tithe on the following occasion.
Rather, the Gemara suggests that Rava derives his halakha from that which is taught in a baraita:
If one erred and called the ninth animal the tenth, and the tenth animal remained in the pen, the ninth animal may be eaten only once it develops a blemish, and the tenth animal is the animal tithe.
The tenth animal has sanctity even though it has not left the pen.

notes.he: אלמא אע"ג דלא יצא קדוש מאליו בדיר. והשתא פריך אהך ברייתא דקתני התשיעי נאכל במומו והתניא וכו':
notes.en: And the tenth is tithe: evidently, even though it did not come out, it is sacred of its own accord in the pen. Now [the Gemara] challenges this baraita, which teaches that the ninth is eaten with its blemish: “But isn’t it taught…”

messages.text: But isn’t it taught in a baraita that in such a case the ninth animal is non-sacred?
messages.quote: the ninth animal may be eaten only once it develops a blemish

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:

notes.he: דתשיעי נאכל במומו ר' שמעון דלא נעקר שם עשירי מעשירי:
notes.en: Whose is this? [The baraita that disagrees] that the ninth is eaten with its blemish is Rabbi Shimon’s, [in a case] where the name of “tenth” was not removed from the tenth.

messages.text: Even the ninth that was accidentally designated as the tenth is not sanctified and may be eaten before it develops a blemish, unless the name of the tenth is removed from the tenth animal, i.e., if the owner erred also in that he called the tenth animal the ninth. And logical reasoning leads to this conclusion.

notes.he: דכי היכי דאם קרא לאחד עשר עשירי אינו קדוש אלא א"כ נעקר שם מעשר מן העשירי שלא קרא לעשירי עשירי אלא תשיעי וכדאמרינן לקמן במתניתין זה הכלל כל שלא נעקר וכו' ובסיפא דהך ברייתא מפרש טעמא משום דאחד עשר עושה קדושה ליקרב א"נ אחד עשר דאיברר כו' אף תשיעי אם קראו עשירי לא יהא נאכל אלא במומו אא"כ נעקר שם העשירי מן העשירי כגון שקראו תשיעי ולהכי הכא דלא נעקר אמרינן דהתשיעי חולין והדין נותן גבי תשיעי נמי בעינן דליהוי נעקר שם עשירי ממנו כלומר מן העשירי עצמו:
notes.en: Even the ninth: just as, if he called the eleventh “tenth”, it is not sacred unless the name of tithe was removed from the tenth, that is, he did not call the tenth “tenth” but “ninth”, as we say below in the mishna (60a), “This is the principle: wherever the name of tenth was not removed…”, and the latter part of this baraita explains the reason, because the eleventh produces sanctity to be sacrificed, or alternatively because with the eleventh [the tenth] was already selected: so too the ninth, if he called it “tenth”, will not be eaten only with its blemish unless the name of the tenth was removed from the tenth, for example he called it “ninth”. Therefore here, where it was not removed, we say the ninth is non-sacred. “And logic dictates”: with the ninth too we require that the name of tenth be removed “from it”, that is, from the tenth itself.

notes.he: שאינו נאכל אלא במומו. אסיפא דמתניתין מיירי:
notes.en: Even the ninth is not sacred: [not sacred] to be eaten only with its blemish. [Rabbi Shimon] speaks of the latter clause of the mishna.

notes.dh: אלא א"כ נעקר שם העשירי הימנו
notes.he: מעשירי דלא קרא לעשירי עשירי אבל קראו עשירי לודאי עשירי התשיעי חולין:
notes.en: Unless the name of the tenth was removed from it: from the tenth, that is, he did not call the tenth “tenth”. But if he called the definite tenth “tenth”, the ninth is non-sacred.

messages.text: The halakha is that if one designated the ninth animal as the tenth, and the tenth as the tenth, and the eleventh as the tenth, then the eleventh is not consecrated. This is because in any situation where the name of the tenth was not removed from the tenth animal, the eleventh, which was called the tenth, is not consecrated.

And if the eleventh animal, which becomes sanctified to be sacrificed as a peace offering, as stated in the mishna on 60a, is sanctified only if the name of the tenth is removed from the tenth animal, then with regard to the ninth animal, which does not become sanctified to be sacrificed but is eaten once it develops a blemish, is it not logical that if the name of the tenth is removed from the actual tenth animal, then yes, the ninth animal has sanctity and may be eaten only once it develops a blemish, but if not, then it is not sanctified at all and may be eaten even without a blemish?

notes.he: כדאמרינן לקמן שאם קרא לאחד עשר עשירי קרב שלמים ומפקינן מקרא ואע"פ שהוא חמור כל כך אינו קדוש אלא א"כ נעקר מן העשירי שם עשירי כגון שקרא לעשירי תשיעי וכדאמרי' לקמן זה הכלל כו':
notes.en: To be sacrificed: as we say below (60a), that if he called the eleventh “tenth” it is sacrificed as a peace offering, and we derive it from a verse. And even though it is so stringent, it is sacred only if the name of tenth was removed from the tenth, for example he called the tenth “ninth”, as we say below: “This is the principle…”

notes.he: שהוא קל כל כך:
notes.en: The ninth: which is so lenient.

notes.he: אע"פ שקראו עשירי אינו קרב אלא קדוש להא מלתא גרידא דאינו נאכל אלא במומו כדלקמן אינו דין וכו':
notes.en: Which does not produce sanctity to be sacrificed: even though he called it “tenth”, it is not sacrificed; it is sacred only for this alone, that it is eaten only with its blemish, as below. Is it not logical, and so on.

notes.he: ליהוי קדוש כלל:
notes.en: If not, not: it would not be sacred at all.

notes.dh: והדין נותן ומה אחד עשר שהוא עושה קדושה ליקרב
notes.he: כדאמרינן במתניתין ואחד עשר קרב שלמים אינו קדוש האחד עשר אלא א"כ נעקר שם העשירי ממנו מן העשירי כדתנן קרא לתשיעי עשירי ולעשירי עשירי:
notes.en: And logic dictates: if the eleventh, which produces sanctity to be sacrificed, as we say in the mishna, “and the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering”, is not sacred unless the name of the tenth was removed from the tenth, as we learned: he called the ninth “tenth” and the tenth “tenth” [and the eleventh “tenth”, the eleventh is not sanctified]…

messages.text: That claim itself provides support for the contrary opinion. With regard to the eleventh animal, which becomes sanctified with a stringent sanctity to be sacrificed as a peace offering, if the name of the tenth is removed from the actual tenth animal, then yes, the eleventh becomes sanctified, but if the designation of being the tenth is not removed from the tenth, then the eleventh does not become sanctified.

notes.he: מהדר הש"ס דודאי גבי תשיעי דין הוא דאע"ג דלא נעקר שם עשירי הימנו דלהוי חל עליה קדושה שלו משום דגבי אחד עשר דין הוא דאי נעקר אין אי לא לא משום דקדושה שלו חמורה היא שהרי קרב כדלקמן ולכך דין הוא דבעינן עקירה עד דתיחול על ההיא קדושה חמורה:
notes.en: That itself provides: the Gemara replies that with the ninth it is certainly logical that its sanctity takes effect on it even though the name of tenth was not removed from [the tenth]. For with the eleventh it is logical that if [the name] was removed, yes, and if not, not, because its sanctity is stringent, as it is sacrificed, as below; so it is logical to require removal before that stringent sanctity takes effect.

notes.he: כלומר מאותו דין שאתה מביא נלמד שהתשיעי ליהוי קדוש אע"פ שלא נעקר שם עשירי מעשירי:
notes.en: That itself provides: that is, from that very argument you bring, we learn that the ninth is sacred even though the name of tenth was not removed from the tenth.

messages.text: But with regard to the ninth animal, which does not become sanctified with the stringent sanctity to be sacrificed, one can say that even though the name of the tenth animal is not removed from the tenth animal, nevertheless the ninth becomes sanctified.

notes.he: דקדושתו קלה דאינו קדוש לקרב אלא שלא יהא נאכל אלא במומו דין הוא דההיא קדושה קלה תיחול בדבר קל כגון דקראו עשירי ואע"ג דלא נעקר שם מעשר מן העשירי עצמו:
notes.en: But the ninth: whose sanctity is light, as it is not sacred to be sacrificed but only so that it is eaten only with its blemish: it is logical that this light sanctity takes effect through a light thing, such as his calling it “tenth”, even though the name of tithe was not removed from the tenth itself.

messages.text: Alternatively, there is another distinction between the two cases. With regard to the eleventh animal, which is sanctified only after the tenth animal has been selected, as it has emerged from the pen, one can claim that if the name of the tenth is removed from the tenth animal, then yes, the eleventh becomes sanctified, but if the name of the tenth is not removed from the tenth animal, the eleventh does not become sanctified.

notes.he: איכא למימר טעמא אחרינא:
notes.en: Alternatively: one can give another reason.

notes.he: שכבר יצא העשירי קודם שיצא האחד עשר ונברר מעצמו שהוא מעשר ולהכי דין הוא דלא ליהוי אחד עשר קדוש אע"פ שקראו עשירי אא"כ נעקר שם מעשר מן העשירי דלאחר עשירי גמור היכי אפשר עשירי אחר בסמוך לו:
notes.en: The eleventh, for which the tenth was selected: the tenth had already come out before the eleventh came out, and was selected of itself as tithe. So it is logical that the eleventh not be sacred even though he called it “tenth”, unless the name of tithe was removed from the tenth: after a complete tenth, how could there be another tenth right next to it?

messages.text: But with regard to the ninth animal, which becomes sanctified at a time when the tenth animal has not yet been selected, as the tenth animal has not yet left the pen, if the owner accidentally designated that ninth animal as the tenth it becomes sanctified, and in such a case this is the halakha even though the name of the tenth animal is not removed from the actual tenth animal.

notes.he: ואזיל וקראו עשירי לזה:
notes.en: Even though he did not remove it: and he went and called this one “tenth”.

notes.he: ליכא למימר בהאי דינא דקאמר היא הנותנת דודאי דין הוא דתיהוי קדוש אע"ג דלא נעקר:
notes.en: There is nothing more: nothing can be said against this argument he made, “that itself provides”, for it is certainly logical that [the ninth] be sacred even though [the name] was not removed.

notes.he: דאכתי לא איברר ליה עשירי שעדיין לא יצא קדוש תשיעי אע"ג דלא נעקר שם עשירי ממנו דלא קרא לו שם אחד שנשאר בדיר:
notes.en: For which the tenth was selected, as it had already come out. [But the ninth,] for which the tenth was not yet selected, as it had not yet come out, is sacred even though the name of tenth was not removed from it, since he did not name the one left in the pen.

messages.text: ✖ There is nothing more to add to that explanation, and the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Shimon is rejected.
A tally fit to reach ten exempts the animals that have been counted from being tithed.

notes.he: שאם היה לו עשרה טלאים והכניסן לדיר ומנה תשעה או שמונה ומת אחד מן הנשארים בדיר או יצא בפתח אחר שלא נתקדש העשירי פטורין אלו שמנה כבר משום דהוו מנין הראוי דבשעה שמנאן היו ראויין אלו שבדיר לצאת ולהתעשר העשירי עם אלו למנין דהשתא משמע לן דהיינו מאותו מנין שלא גמר עדיין שלא מנה אלא תשעה או שמנה כדפרישנא לעיל:
notes.en: A fit tally exempts: if he had ten lambs, brought them into the pen and counted nine or eight, and one of those remaining in the pen died, or went out through another opening so that the tenth was not sanctified, those he already counted are exempt because they are a fit tally: when he counted them, those in the pen were fit to come out and the tenth be tithed together with these for the count. Here it implies to us that [the exemption] is from that same count, which he has not yet completed, having counted only nine or eight, as I explained above.

messages.text: From where does Rava derive this halakha? If we say he derives it from that which we learned in the mishna, this is problematic. The Gemara cites the relevant statement of the mishna:
messages.quote: A tally fit to reach ten exempts

messages.text: If before one completed tithing his animals, one of those counted jumped back into the pen among the animals that were not yet counted, all those in the pen are exempt from being tithed, as each of them could be the animal that was already counted.

notes.he: בדיר כולן פטורין משום דאיערב דהנהו שמנוין כבר פטורין אע"פ שעדיין לא עישר עליהן:
notes.en: Among them: into the pen. All are exempt because they became mixed, for those already counted are exempt even though he has not yet tithed for them.

messages.text: With regard to this halakha concerning which the counted animals themselves are exempt, is it not because they were counted with a tally fit to reach ten?
messages.quote: all those in the pen are exempt

notes.he: שכשיצאו מן הדיר עדיין נשאר בדיר שהיה יכול להשלים מנינן:
notes.en: Is it not that they were exempted through a fit tally: when they came out of the pen, there was still [an animal] left in the pen that could complete their count.

messages.text: But perhaps this is referring to a case where the tenth animal also came out of the pen, and the owner tithed it on behalf of the others that were counted. If so, they are not exempt simply because they were counted with a tally fit to reach ten but because they were actually tithed.

notes.he: והיינו מן המנויין כלומר מאותן שמנה ועישר עליהן:
notes.en: But perhaps he tithed for them: and that is what “from the counted” means, that is, from those he counted and tithed for.

notes.he: מהכא לא מצית דדילמא מהנהו מנויין קאמר דקפץ לתוכו הנהו דכבר עישר עלייהו:
notes.en: But perhaps: you cannot [prove it] from here, for perhaps it speaks of counted animals for which he had already tithed, which jumped in.

messages.text: You cannot say that the mishna is addressing a situation where one of the animals for which tithe had already been separated jumped back in, as the latter clause of the mishna teaches: If one of those animals that had been tithed jumped back into the pen among the animals that were not yet counted. This indicates that in the situation described in the first clause the animals had been counted but not yet tithed.

notes.he: דהדר קתני לה מן המעושרין אלמא דהאי מנויין דקאמר דלאו מעושרין נינהו:
notes.en: You cannot say that: for it goes on to teach “from the tithed”; evidently the “counted” it speaks of are not tithed.

messages.text: But perhaps, what is the meaning of the term: Animals that had been tithed? This is referring specifically to the tenth animal, which is the actual tithe.

notes.he: כלומר מן המעשרות עצמן:
notes.en: Tithed: that is, from the tithes themselves.

notes.he: ודלמא מאי מן המעושרין דקאמר שקפץ מעשר עצמו לתוכו:
notes.en: But perhaps, what does “from the tithed” mean? That the tithe itself jumped in.

messages.text: And accordingly, the language of the mishna is also precise, as it teaches: All the animals must graze until they become unfit for sacrifice, and thereafter they may be eaten in their blemished state by their owner. Concerning animal tithe, this halakha applies specifically to the tenth animal when it reentered the pen, and not to the other nine. Therefore, the Gemara has not yet found a source for Rava’s halakha.

notes.he: משום דכל חד וחד איכא לספוקי דהיינו הוא המעשר:
notes.en: Must graze: because about each and every one there is a doubt that it is the tithe.

notes.he: דכולהו הוי ספק מעשר. והאי מן המנויין דקאמר מהנך דכבר עישר עליהן ואכתי לא מצי יליף מהכא דמנין הראוי פוטר:
notes.en: It is also precise, since it teaches “must graze”: for all of them are possibly tithe. And “from the counted” refers to those for which he had already tithed. So we still cannot derive from here that a fit tally exempts.

messages.text: the verse states: “Whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be sacred to the Lord.” This indicates that only an animal that will pass under the rod must be tithed, but not an animal that has already passed under the rod.

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: אלא אמר רבא מקרא יליף דכתיב יעבר ולא שכבר עבר:
notes.en: Rather, Rava said: he derives it from a verse, as it is written “passes”, and not what has already passed.

messages.text: What is the meaning of: An animal that has already passed? If it means that one has separated tithe for it, is it necessary for a verse to state this? Of course an animal that has been tithed does not need to be tithed again. Rather, is it not referring to a case where the animals have become exempt through a tally fit to reach ten? Conclude from this that a tally fit to reach ten renders an animal exempt from being tithed.

notes.he: דהכי משמע ולא שכבר עבר בראוי דבשעה שעבר היה ראוי להתעשר מאלו שבדיר דההוא ודאי משום דאיפטר במנין הראוי:
notes.en: Rather, is it not that they were exempted, and so on: for this is what it implies: “and not that which already passed” through a fit [tally], that at the time it passed it was fit to be tithed together with those in the pen; that one is certainly [exempt], because it was exempted through a fit tally.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rava:

In a case where one had ten lambs and he brought them into the pen and counted five, and then one of them died, if one of those animals that had been counted died, he continues to count and completes the tithe for them. But if one of the animals that had not been counted died, those animals that had been counted are exempt, and those animals that had not been counted combine with animals born later, to be tithed in another designated time of gathering.

notes.he: לאו דוקא נקט ה':
notes.en: And he counted five: “five” is not meant precisely.

notes.he: משום דהוו מנין הראוי:
notes.en: The counted are exempt: because they were a fit tally.

notes.he: מאותן שיצאו מן הדיר מה בכך מונה ומשלים עליהם ועל אותו שמת עד שיהו עשרה ויפריש אחד:
notes.en: If one of the counted died: of those that came out of the pen, what of it? He counts and completes over them and over the one that died until there are ten, and separates one.

notes.he: מהנך שבדיר:
notes.en: And if one of those not counted died: of those in the pen.

notes.he: שפטרן מנין הראוי שבשעה שיצאו עדיין לא מת והיה ראוי להשלים מניינן לעשרה ושאינן מנויין אותן שנשתיירו בדיר הארבע' לא ניפטרו אלא מצטרפין לגורן אחד לעשרו עם שאר בהמות:
notes.en: The counted that went outside are exempt: the fit tally exempted them, for when they came out [the one] had not yet died and was fit to complete their count to ten. And those not counted, the four left in the pen, are not exempted but combine for another gathering, to be tithed with other animals.

messages.text: In a case where one had fourteen lambs and brought them into the pen, and six of the lambs emerged first, through this opening on one side of the pen, and four lambs emerged afterward through that opening on the other side of the pen, and four lambs remained there,

notes.he: שהיה לדיר שני פתחים:
notes.en: Through this opening: for the pen had two openings.

messages.text: if those four that remained came out by the opening through which the six lambs emerged, he takes the last one of them as animal tithe. And the remainder, i.e., the four that emerged through the other opening, combine with animals born later, to be tithed in another designated time of gathering.

notes.he: דהואיל ויצאו עשרה באותו פתח:
notes.en: He takes one of them: since ten came out through that opening.

notes.he: הארבעה שיצאו בפתח אחר מצטרפין לגורן אחר דבמנין הראוי לא אפשר למפטרינהו להני משום שבשעה שיצאו בפתח אחד לא היה מנין ראוי דלא נשתיירו בדיר אלא ד' וד' לא אפשר לאיצטרופי לד' דליהוו בני עשורי:
notes.en: And the remainder: the four that came out through the other opening combine for another gathering. They cannot be exempted through a fit tally, for when they came out through their opening there was no fit tally: only four were left in the pen, and four with four cannot combine to be subject to tithe.

messages.text: But if not, i.e., if the last four remained in the pen or came out through the same opening through which the other four lambs emerged, then the six that emerged first are exempt from animal tithe, as they were part of a tally fit to reach ten; and the four that came out next, from the other opening, and the last four, combine with animals born later, to be tithed in another designated time of gathering.

notes.he: שלא יצאו הארבעה בפתח הששה אלא או נשתיירו בדיר או יצאו בפתח הארבעה אחרים:
notes.en: But if not: the four did not come out through the opening of the six, but either remained in the pen or came out through the opening of the other four.

notes.he: שלא יצאו בפתח שיצאו ששה אלא בפתח ארבעה דהשתא הוו שמונה ולא חזו למעשר:
notes.en: But if not: they did not come out through the opening where the six came out but through the opening of the four, so that now there are eight [there], not fit for tithe.

notes.he: משום דבשעה שיצאו מן הדיר נשתייר בדיר מנין הראוי להשלימן לעשרה והנך ארבעה ואינך ארבעה מצטרפין לגורן אחד:
notes.en: The six that came out first are exempt: because when they came out of the pen, there remained in the pen a count fit to complete them to ten. And these four and those four combine for another gathering.

messages.text: In a case where four of the fourteen lambs emerged first, through this opening on one side of the pen, and six lambs came out afterward through that other opening, and four lambs remained there, if those four that remained come out by the opening through which the six lambs emerged, the owner takes the last one of them as animal tithe, and the remainder, i.e., the four that went out of the other opening, are exempt, as they were part of a tally fit to reach ten.

notes.he: תחלה בפתח זה כו':
notes.en: Four came out: first, through this opening, and so on.

notes.he: אפילו אותן ארבעה שיצאו תחלה משום דאינהו נפטרו במנין הראוי:
notes.en: He takes one as tithe and the rest are exempt: even the four that came out first, because they were exempted through a fit tally.

messages.text: But if not, i.e., if the last four emerge via the same opening as the first four, the four that came out first and the six that emerged through the other opening are exempt, as there were enough lambs left to complete the ten when all these left. And the four that went out last combine with animals born later, to be tithed in another designated time of gathering.

notes.he: משום דכי יצאו הארבעה תחלה הוו מנין ראוי דאכתי אישתייר בדיר עשרה שראוין להצטרף להם ולעשר עליהם וארבעה אחרונים שנשתיירו או יצאו בפתח שלישי מצטרפין לגורן אחר:
notes.en: The first four and the six are exempt: because when the four came out first they were a fit tally, for ten still remained in the pen, fit to combine with them and be tithed for them. And the last four, which remained or came out through a third opening, combine for another gathering. [This note explains the second case, Rava’s “but if not” in 59b14.]

notes.he: שלא יצאו אלא בפתח הארבעה ד' ראשונים וו' שניים פטורין משום דנשתייר בדיר שראוי להשלימן:
notes.en: But if not: [the last four] came out only through the opening of the four. The first four and the second six are exempt, because there remained in the pen [enough] fit to complete them.

notes.he: והנך ד' אחרונים מצטרפין לגורן אחד:
notes.en: And these last four combine for another gathering.

messages.text: In a case where four of the fourteen lambs emerged first, through this opening, and four lambs came out afterward through that other opening, and six lambs remained there, if those six that remained come out through any one opening, he takes one of them as animal tithe, and the remainder, i.e., the four that went out of the other opening, are exempt, as they were part of a tally fit to reach ten.

notes.dh: אם אותן ששה שנשתיירו יצאו בפתח אחד מהן
notes.he: כלומר בפתח הארבעה הראשונים או בפתח הד' האחרונים:
notes.en: If those six that remained came out through one of their openings: that is, through the opening of the first four or through the opening of the last four.

notes.he: דהוו י' בפתח אחד:
notes.en: He takes one of them: because there are ten at one opening.

notes.dh: אם אותן ששה כולם בפתח אחד יצאו
notes.he: או בפתח ד' ראשונים או בפתח ד' שניים הוו י' ונוטל מהן אחד והשאר פטורין כולן אפילו אותן ד' שלא יצאו הו' בפתחן משום דאותן [ד' שניים נמי] כי יצאו הוו להו מנין הראוי ואם לאו ששלשה מהן יצאו בפתח זה וג' בפתח זה הד' ד' פטורין משום דיצאו במנין הראוי והו' מצטרף לגורן אחד:
notes.en: If those six all came out through one opening, either the opening of the first four or that of the second four, there are ten and he takes one of them, and all the rest are exempt, even the four through whose opening the six did not come out, because those [second four too], when they came out, were a fit tally. But if not, three of them came out through this opening and three through that one: each four is exempt, because they came out in a fit tally, and the six combine for another gathering.

messages.text: But if not, i.e., if the six remain in the pen, the four sheep that emerged on this side and the four that came out on that side are exempt. And the six that remain combine with animals born later, to be tithed in another designated time of gathering.

notes.he: שלא יצאו לא בפתח אלו ד' ולא בפתח אלו ד' אלא בפני עצמן או נשתיירו בדיר:
notes.en: But if not: they came out neither through the opening of these four nor through the opening of those four, but by themselves, or they remained in the pen.

notes.he: דכל ד' וד' שיצאו הניחו אחרים כדי להצטרף להן ולהתעשר עליהן דהנהו ששה שנשתיירו שדינן בין להכא בין להכא:
notes.en: The first four and the last four are exempt: for each group of four that came out left others behind enough to combine with them and be tithed for them, since the six that remained can be assigned both here and there.

messages.caption: Rava’s fourteen lambs in a pen with two openings: where the last group goes out decides which lambs are tithed, which are exempt by a tally fit to reach ten, and which wait for the next gathering.

messages.text: What is Rava teaching us? Is he teaching that any animal that comes out of the pen as part of a tally fit to reach ten is exempt? But didn’t Rava say that already once?
messages.quote: one had fourteen lambs and brought them into the pen

messages.text: Rava’s statement is necessary, lest you say that only if the animals emerge as part of a tally that is definitely fit to reach ten do we say they are exempt. But if they come out as part of a tally with regard to which it is uncertain whether it is fit to reach ten, such as in this case where the remaining animals are fit to come out here and are fit to come out there, and therefore the first animals might not be part of a counting that will reach ten, we do not say they are exempt. Therefore, Rava teaches us that even a tally that is uncertain to reach ten exempts the animals from tithe.

notes.he: כגון שמנה ה' או ו' ונשתיירו בדיר כדי לצרף להן וליכא בדיר אלא אותו פתח דוודאי הוא דאותן שנשתיירו ראויין לצאת דרך אותו פתח עצמו ולהתעשר עם אלו שמנה כבר:
notes.en: A definitely fit tally: for example, he counted five or six and enough remained in the pen to combine with them, and the pen has only that opening, so it is certain that those remaining are fit to come out through that same opening and be tithed together with those he already counted.

notes.he: כגון שיצאו בשני פתחים ארבעה בפתח זה וארבעה בפתח זה דהנך ששה שנשתיירו ליכא למיקם עלייהו אי יצאו בפתח זה או בפתח זה וכיון דספק הוא אימא דלא אמרינן מנין הראוי למישדינהו בין להכא בין להכא לפטור את כולן קמשמע לן. ענין אחר הא דחזו הנך להכא ולהכא דשדינן להו בין להנך ארבע בין להנך ארבע היינו חשוב ספק. ומפי המורה:
notes.en: But an uncertainly fit tally: for example, they came out through two openings, four through this opening and four through that one; with the six that remained, one cannot determine whether they will come out through this opening or that. Since it is uncertain, one might say we do not apply “fit tally” and assign them both here and there to exempt them all. [Rava] teaches us [that we do]. Another explanation: the very fact that they are fit for here and for there, so that we assign them both to these four and to those four, is what counts as “uncertain”. This is from the mouth of my teacher.

notes.dh: מהו דתימא ודאי מנין הראוי אמרינן
notes.he: כגון היכא דיצאו ו' בפתח זה וד' בפתח זה וד' נשתיירו דודאי דהנהו ד' דנשתיירו לא חזו לאיצטרופי אלא [עם] הששה. אבל ספק מנין הראוי כגון כשנשתיירו ו' בדיר דחזו לאיצטרופי בין להני ד' בין להני ד' ולא ידעינן להי מצטרפי אימא לא קמ"ל:
notes.en: Lest you say we apply only a definitely fit tally: for example, where six came out through this opening and four through that one, and four remained, it is certain that the four that remained are fit to combine only [with] the six. But an uncertainly fit tally, as when six remained in the pen, fit to combine either with these four or with those four, and we do not know with which: say we do not. [Rava] teaches us [that we do].

messages.text: If one had fifteen lambs, he may not say: I will separate ten and bring them into the pen, and I will take one of them as animal tithe, and the rest will be exempt. Rather, he must bring them all into the pen, and remove ten of them by causing them to emerge from the opening, and take one of them, i.e., the one that emerges tenth, as animal tithe. And the remainder combine with animals born later, to be tithed in another designated time of gathering.

notes.he: לא נקט משום דווקא אלא אורחא דמילתא לצרופי חמשה בהדי חמשה:
notes.en: Fifteen lambs: not meant precisely; it is just the usual way of putting it, combining five with five.

notes.he: הנהו ה' נמי שלא הכניס משום דלית בהו שעור מעשר אלא יעשה להן דבר שיתחייבו במעשר כולן יכניסם (כולן) לדיר ויוציא עשרה ויטול מהן א' והשאר הה' מאחר שנכנסו בדיר ואין בהן שעור מעשר הדיר קובעו ומצטרפין לגורן אחד:
notes.en: And the rest are exempt: [he would claim] the five he did not bring in are exempt too, since they lack the minimum for tithe. Rather, let him act so that they all become obligated in tithe: bring them all into the pen, take out ten and take one of them; and the remaining five, since they entered the pen while lacking the minimum for tithe, the pen fixes them [as obligated], and they combine for another gathering.

messages.text: This is also taught in a baraita:
If one had fifteen lambs, …
The baraita on fifteen lambs continues on 60a, where the Gemara sets it against a baraita about nineteen lambs.
